Val: The Tiny Town with a Big Heart

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Nestled in the open fields of Mpumalanga lies Val, South Africa’s smallest town. With its population barely reaching double digits, Val is a place where time seems to stand still. But behind its qua

Unique Selling Point:
Val isn’t just a town—it’s a glimpse into South Africa’s rural heritage, made vibrant by a one-woman mission to keep its stories alive. This narrative weaves the charm of small-town life with the universal appeal of resilience, history, and nostalgia.

Summary:
This story explores Val’s journey from a forgotten railway town to a living time capsule. We meet Rita Brits, the spirited woman at the heart of Val’s preservation, whose passion has transformed it into a historical gem and a haven for artists and wanderers. From meticulously restored buildings to tales of bygone eras, Val embodies the power of preservation and community spirit.

Further information:
Suggested Cinematics:
• Wide shots of Val’s serene, open landscapes contrasted with its charming streets.
• Close-ups of Rita tending to restored structures or sharing tales with visitors.
• Archival photos of Val in its heyday, blending seamlessly with present-day visuals.
• Interviews with locals, travellers, and artists who found inspiration in Val.

Script:


- Country’s smallest town.

– Driving visuals–

Link Macfarlane : So we are on a roadtrip to try and find South Africa’s smallest town, apparently there are eight people there, it's called Val..No Vaal…Maybe 8 people fell there…and is it a town or a hamlet ? Lat ons eit gaan find.
[ breather / roadtrip visuals]

1.V/O Just a 90-minute drive from Johannesburg and 30 minutes from Heidelberg, Val sits quietly in the Highveld platteland.

Link Macfarlane : So is this it , is it really it …but listen…silence.


2.V/O After roaming the streets and spotting no one, I made my way to the local pub, The [clears throat] Moeggeploeg Kroeg, to meet Val’s unofficial mayor, historian, and probably its bouncer too—Rita Britz.

Upsound Mac 07:08 : This place has got the title of the smallest town. Is this even a town?

Upsound Rita : 07 20 we love referring it to as a hamlet. It sounds so romantic. We can't do that in Afrikaans because its called a Gehegie, gehegie and that is not romantic.

Upsound Rita 12 :35 We are only 8 inhabitants, and 100% employment rate, and 28 policemen.

Upsound Rita 07:20 So we have a church, We have a hotel.Police station and bar.

[transition historic pictures ]

3.V/O Val started as a humble stagecoach stop, it soon grew into a tiny town when the Johannesburg-Durban railway line was built in 1896.

Upsound Rita 03 :11 Val started a very thriving community with the station. English and Afrikaans families,9And they were next door neighbours, they were interacting, having parties together with others.

[breather]
4 V/O Oh! but Tiny Val holds big stories: Boer General Louis Botha declared the South African War unwinnable here in 1902, and Mahatma Gandhi was famously arrested during a peaceful march through the town. Renowned photographer Wessel Oosthuizen grew up surrounded by tales of Gandhi's arrest.

Upsound Wessel he was brought back and he was locked up at the police station, which was just across the railway lines here. Oh, just here? Yeah,[ breather] unfortunately. It was demolished.

Upsound Wessel A lot of people moved away f. They go into the cities, especially the young people, because there's no future for them here. There's no work for them in a place like this. Foll, fortunately.


5 V/O In the 90s, Val was on the verge of becoming a ghost town—Until Rita spotted a then rundown Val hotel up for sale in 1994.

Upsound Rita // Nobody wanted it. It was so derelict and dirty and unloved. really terrible.

6V/O She decided to quit her teaching job and cash in her pension, and bought the hotel for just R 18 000.

Upsound Rita : 22:18 So it took us eight months to restore it.

Upsound Rita 8:02 To know the locals support us.the whole spirit of the community is when we stand together, we stand together like
One.

7V/O With this Val was reborn.
[transition]

8V/O For fourth-generation farmer Brett Gordon, Val’s strong sense of community has been his lifeline.

Upsound Brett Gordon 03:22it's the population decreasing in the rural areas, getting ever less. So I look at our neighbours and I look at the guys in our farmers association, we're like a family. And we've got to help each other
[transition]

9 V/O Speaking of work; in true Platteland style, Brett had a job for me: catching sheep!"

[transition ]

Link Mac day 2 : So the tradition in Val is that if you hang up your shoes , you are going to be here forever and you are not going to go home, if you fall in love with the place it actually feels that way.



[ end]


Promos 1:

VO: Nestled in the heart of the Highveld, the tiny town of Val is anything but ordinary.

Upsound Rita 12 :35 We are only 8 inhabitants, and 100% employment rate, and 28 policemen. So we have a church, t. We have a hotel.Police station and bar.

V/O So what do you do in a dorpie with just 8 people…well


Promo 2:

V/O Val in Mpumalanga may be small with 8 permanent residents , but its heart and stories are larger than life.

Upsound Rita : Gandhi came to townr. That was a very big thing. Gandhi came on his peace march from... the crowd became so big that the police feared that there would be riot.

V/O I'm taking a road trip to find out what makes Val truly unforgettable.





Promo 3 :

VO: What’s life like in a town with only eight people? In Val, it’s a mix of history, humor, and unexpected surprises.
Upsound Rita: Upsound Rita 12 :35 Upsound Rita : 07 20 Yeah, we love referring it to as a hamlet. It sounds so romantic. // 07:52 We can't do that in Afrikaans because its called a Gehegie, gehegie and that is not romantic.
VO: I explore—a small town with a big personality.
